data.name: Jammaz
data.gender_notes: Jammaz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘jam’ which means grapes, this name signifies richness, fullness, and abundance. It is a name of great significance for parents who wish to bless their child with a rich and prosperous future. The name Jammaz carries the meaning “Grapes” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Jammaz usually hope their child will grow to embody grapes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Jammaz signifies the sweetness and richness of life, as well as the blessings and rewards of hard work and dedication. It is a reminder to cherish the present moment and to strive for growth and abundance in all areas of life.
data.etymology: Jammaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grapes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jammaz total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.context: Jammaz ibn Jabor was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the first governor of Kufa after the death of Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He is also known for leading the first major military campaign against the Byzantines in 633 AD, resulting in the capture of Damascus.

historical_references.context: Jammaz ibn Artat was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and a prominent member of the Ansar of Medina. He is also known for leading a military expedition to Syria in 634 AD, which resulted in the capture of Hims, one of the major Roman cities.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic name 'Jammaz', which signifies a state of purification before undertaking the Hajj pilgrimage, has evolved to encompass a broader meaning in modern times. During the holy month of Ramadan, the term 'Jammaz' is often used metaphorically to refer to individuals who have spiritually prepared themselves for the month-long period of fasting, prayer, and charitable giving. This preparation includes participating in Iftar parties, engaging in daily prayer, and making charitable donations. Social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook are popular avenues for sharing experiences, photos, and messages related to Ramadan and the Jammaz lifestyle.
